description: Read-only operator known-issues corpus served by wiki agent-faq. Recovery uses current intent-specific tools within session grants and producer-returned references. Entries identify the responsible actor; this corpus grants no authority. Authoring, action preview, integration and publication require coordinator grants; workers read their assignment and request assignment correction for missing required context.

entries.title: Worker reports its read-first references are missing, or read_scope vs docs: is unfamiliar
entries.symptom: A worker reports that its read-first references are missing or empty; lint reports `missing_docs_target` or an unresolved `read_scope` entry; or you set the WK's `docs:` field and the worker expected `read_scope`.
entries.cause: read_scope names the durable read-first references for the work record or slice. Missing or stale references require an explicit authored correction; use the saved unit input contract, not a historical field alias.

routes.note: Coordinator: read the exact unit with workspace_read_wiki and select its returned save_record input contract for read_scope. Author the complete intended correction. A managed worker uses assignment:true to read its frozen assignment and request_assignment_change with its own gap evidence and completed/remaining work; acceptance ends that worker immediately.

entries.title: Graph impact required but unavailable or stale
entries.symptom: `start_agent preview` or `start_agent preview` reports graph impact required but unavailable, or you hit a `missing_graph_impact` / `graph_impact_*` blocker.
entries.cause: Graph-dependent operations automatically ensure the shared committed-HEAD index. Missing, stale, corrupt, and incompatible cache state normally rebuilds through the incumbent atomic/coalesced owner and the requesting operation continues. A remaining unavailable result therefore means the actual rebuild, verification, or captured-HEAD stabilization failed; dirty-worktree content is never substituted for the committed base.

routes.note: Retry the original graph-dependent operation after correcting the reported rebuild cause. The original operation strictly ensures the shared committed index again; a separate status/build discovery round trip is not required. query_code_index reads the published index immediately and requests background refresh through the existing owner.

fork.when: graph_impact_degraded_overlay: a dirty worktree with a usable overlay is available (the proceed_degraded outcome).

routes.note: Query committed impact for the changed paths; dirty worktree bytes stay excluded from the committed graph and are only disclosed.
Assess the original unit after the reported graph prerequisite is repaired. Do not copy a compact query answer into canonical evidence or substitute dirty data for the committed base.

fork.note: Agent-recoverable. Do not request an operator rebuild for this sub-state; the overlay is usable, so persist real evidence from it.

fork.when: graph_impact_unavailable after automatic ensure: the returned cause names a real builder, cache-publication, repository, or unstable-HEAD failure.

routes.note: After the named cause is corrected, retry the original graph-dependent operation. The original operation strictly ensures the shared committed index again, including rebuild when required. query_code_index reads the published index immediately and requests background refresh through the existing owner.

fork.note: Do not substitute stale or dirty-overlay data for a failed committed build. Report the exact returned cause when its correction requires operator access.

entries.title: Graph evidence cannot be established for the selected unit
entries.symptom: The selected action reports missing or unusable committed graph evidence.
entries.cause: Read the original refusal and repair its specific index or graph prerequisite. query_code_index explains changed-path impact from the published index; its compact projection is not a canonical evidence payload. Reassess the selected unit after correction rather than copying query output into a retired evidence request.

routes.note: Ask change impact using paths, patchText, diffRecords or liveGit:true. Follow its returned references for complete derived evidence; do not treat a compact summary as a canonical write carrier.
Assess the original unit after the reported graph prerequisite is repaired. Do not copy a compact query answer into canonical evidence or substitute dirty data for the committed base.

entries.title: needs_review on write_scope_total_loc / max_write_file_loc when a small edit targets a large file
entries.symptom: `start_agent` or `start_agent preview` returns a Chassis Control Engine `needs_review` worker-admission result on `write_scope_total_loc` or `max_write_file_loc` (the reason often reads like `review_threshold_exceeded` or an accepted-authority-scope-mismatch on the large-file LOC), even though the actual change is a small, bounded edit inside an otherwise large file.
entries.cause: Admission scored the WHOLE-FILE line count of the large `write_scope` file against the review threshold because the selected unit declared no bounded target plan. Without `expected_edit_targets` + `expected_changed_line_budget`, the gate has nothing narrower than the file's total LOC to reason about, so it routes the small edit into review-threshold pressure. This is a missing-target-evidence gap, not (by itself) a reject, a license/escalation problem, or a graph-impact problem.

entries.title: validate_dispatch non-dispatchable on multi_cluster or critical_blast_radius_*
entries.symptom: start_agent preview reports the selected unit non-dispatchable with decision code `multi_cluster` (the unit's write_scope spans more than one cohesive change cluster) or a `critical_blast_radius_*` code (the change reaches a critical surface with no current, in-scope accepted escalation).
entries.cause: Both are LOCAL dispatch-readiness structural gates an agent can see before any launch — not Node-Engine threshold verdicts — so they need no paid tool. multi_cluster wants one cohesive write_scope cluster per unit; critical_blast_radius_* wants a recorded, accepted, in-scope `critical_blast_radius` escalation whose scope matches the change.

entries.title: A requested validation target is outside the selected contract
entries.symptom: Execution refuses because the requested target or source is not authorized by the selected proof or session.
entries.cause: Saved proof execution uses verify_proof with a saved subject and its authenticated source. Ordinary workspace_run_test accepts frozen worker entrypoint/selection IDs or a nonworker harness within session authority and supplies no proof credit. Repair the named saved test case through its returned authoring contract when that is the failing boundary; a note or ordinary test run does not authorize a proof.

routes.note: Use an assigned worker entrypoint/selection or a nonworker harness within your session source authority. To execute a saved proof, use verify_proof with its saved subject instead; author corrections through the returned save_record contract. A test run grants no proof credit.

entries.title: worker-admission breadth refusal on write_scope_count or validation_command_count
entries.symptom: start_agent or start_agent preview returns a Chassis Control Engine breadth refusal keyed on control_id `write_scope_count` or `validation_command_count` (e.g. `worker_admission.work_unit_atomicity.write_scope_count_denied.v1`): the unit declares too many write_scope files or too many validation commands for one atomic unit.
entries.cause: These are Node-Engine-owned breadth thresholds over the raw carrier metrics (write-scope file breadth / validation-command breadth). Under DEC-0125 large-file / breadth admissibility is CCE-exclusive, so only the paid_cce tier reaches this refusal (a free/local agent fails open). The remedy is to split the unit, not to loosen a threshold.

routes.note: Read the exact unit with workspace_read_wiki, then follow its returned reference to the save_record input contract for the needed members. Author the complete intended correction using that contract; do not infer replacement values. Narrow scope or split the unit before reassessment.

entries.title: Exact-slice reviewer dispatch refuses a stale frozen contract context
entries.symptom: start_agent for an exact-slice reviewer refuses with frozen_slice_review_context_stale_or_mismatched after coordinator bookkeeping changed the canonical parent WK or selected review-unit contract while the committed delivery stayed unchanged.
entries.cause: The hot backend still selected a process-local frozen review context carrying the earlier broad parent-WK or review-unit contract snapshot. The ordinary exact reviewer dispatch can reauthenticate and replace that selection only when reviewed SHA, accumulated diff base, slice ref, worktree identity and path, repository identity, and committed-target digest all remain identical. Delivery movement, selected-unit movement, an object-store probe failure, or any unauthenticated identity remains fail-closed and is not retry-authorized.

routes.note: Retry the ordinary reviewer dispatch for the exact canonical slice subject only when the closed recovery_action is retry_exact_reviewer_dispatch. The backend reauthenticates the same delivery and refreshes only its process-local current contract selection before the unchanged launch guard runs. Do not supply a SHA, digest, path, context, or recovery claim, and do not retry target or identity movement as contract staleness.

entries.title: Terminal candidate is stale against current W
entries.symptom: Candidate inspection reports that the selected version is stale against the observed workspace base.
entries.cause: A stale candidate needs advancement to the observed workspace base. Inspect the candidate, then use the exact returned version_identity as version in workspace_advance_candidate. Review the resulting candidate before publication.

routes.note: Inspect the current candidate. Advance only the explicitly selected version_identity returned by inspection; do not invent a version or copy a Git SHA.

entries.title: Terminal candidate divergence continuation is invalid or stale
entries.symptom: A divergence page continuation is refused as invalid or stale.
entries.cause: The previous observation or continuation no longer selects the current candidate. Inspect again and follow the fresh producer-returned references; inspection repairs nothing and authorizes no advance.

routes.note: Inspect again. Use only fresh producer-returned references and an explicit candidate version for any subsequent advance.

entries.title: Terminal whole-WK review is dispositioned and the candidate is unpublished
entries.symptom: The one terminal whole-WK findings-only review of the exact candidate is finished and every surviving finding is dispositioned, and the next structured action for getting that exact reviewed candidate onto the forge is unclear.
entries.cause: After the exact terminal whole-WK review and disposition, workspace_publish_work publishes the already-reviewed candidate byte-for-byte against the configured base branch to the configured destination. On a hosted destination it creates or observes the pull request; a local/Git destination hands off for human Git landing. Publication neither merges, observes merge state, reconstructs the candidate nor completes work. workspace_check_landing observes landing separately. The closed request is subject only; repository, candidate, branches and destination are configured by the owner. Preserve typed refusals; no shell or gh recovery substitutes for this boundary. Typed refusals include wk_forge_handoff_subject_invalid for an invalid WK subject, wk_forge_handoff_executor_unavailable for a missing configured adapter, and terminal_candidate_recovery_current_ref_absent for an unavailable authenticated current selection. Other owner refusals remain possible.

routes.note: After exact review and disposition, publish the current selection to its configured destination. Supply only subject; preserve any typed refusal and its owning recovery.

entries.title: verify_proof reports an execution or receipt prerequisite failure
entries.symptom: verify_proof returns a workspace-verify-proof-refusal.v1 execution, provider, observation, or receipt code instead of a proof outcome.
entries.cause: A valid structured run of the predeclared selected assertion is proof evidence: a passing assertion may prove the proof and a failing assertion leaves it unproven, independently of sibling assertions and the whole-file exit code. Siblings remain bounded audit observations and are not attributed to the proof. not_executable or refused instead means the selected proof could not be evaluated because a canonical binding, launcher isolation/spawn/timeout prerequisite, structured node:test reporter protocol, candidate/falsifier/traversal provider, candidate identity, or authenticated receipt failed. Ordinary validation diagnostics use bounded head/tail capture. The proof reporter uses a separate lossless machine-protocol channel on a launcher-owned pipe with its own fixed byte limit and is never parsed after diagnostic elision. test_proof_structured_events_oversized means the authenticated envelope exceeded that protocol limit; reduce the declared test's structured event population or repair the reporter protocol owner before retrying, without treating the bytes as malformed JSON. test_proof_selected_identity_not_observed means the authenticated whole-file run terminated or completed without exposing the selected assertion; use its expected_test_id, target, bounded counts, wrapper status/error codes, and at most eight observed_identity_candidates to repair test startup or reporter observation before retrying. test_proof_bound_identity_mismatch is reserved for a genuine disagreement between the declared identity and its authenticated binding; repair the canonical file/name/nesting identity or the shared identity owner. Read the bounded outer_wrapper_code, deepest_stable_cause_code, execution_stage, declared_target, verification_id, test_proof_id, run disposition, blocker/observation code, and truncation facts in the response. Repair a binding or declared test in the controlled proof contract when those facts name the contract boundary; repair the launcher/runtime or reporter/provider prerequisite when they name execution infrastructure. A completed verification returns the compact workspace-verify-proof-summary.v1: requested subject, one common subject binding, aggregate status, exact proof and obligation-relationship counts, per-proof and per-obligation verdicts, shared reason/recovery entries for unmet or unevaluated items, and next_calls naming the exact read of each returned failure. Follow get_run_result calls with the returned result locator and proof selector unchanged to read settled failure details without executing again. Large expected/actual operands stay in the retained result and are reported as deferred with their type and size. A managed worker reads its recorded invocation through get_run_result with assigned:true and the producer-returned recorded_invocation. Raw stdout/stderr and private provider payloads remain outside the public proof result.

routes.note: After repairing the named owner prerequisite, explicitly retry the saved subject. Source selection belongs to the authenticated session; do not add gitSha or git_sha. Read settled originals using the returned get_run_result calls.

entries.title: Worker redispatch finds an existing committed slice delivery
entries.symptom: start_agent refuses a worker call with managed_run_prior_attempt_proven_dead for a slice whose prior attempt already committed a delivery.
entries.cause: A committed delivery is integrated explicitly using its authenticated delivery reference returned by get_run_result. Do not redispatch a worker merely to repeat an already committed delivery, and do not invent a receipt from a subject or SHA. This observation is not an integration decision: integrate_work independently authenticates the delivery. Runtime recovery that requires integration before remediation continues in a follow-up slice of the same WK; no replacement worker is launched by a result read.

routes.note: Read the exact attempt and follow its integrate_work call with the producer-returned delivery reference. Preserve integration refusals and role restrictions.

entries.title: Claude permission configuration and empirical testing
entries.symptom: Does normal Claude launch empirically test native permissions?
entries.cause: Normal worker/reviewer and headless orchestrator launch mint and validate native permission settings, apply settings isolation and preserve scope/confinement, executable checks, credentials/network configuration, MCP readiness and supervision. Redteam remains settings-free and probe-free. Applied configuration is not empirical certification: ordinary launch runs no auxiliary Claude permission test and needs no report, canary or positive cache. Genuine setup failures retain their stage-specific diagnostics. Empirical checks belong to explicitly opted-in integration tests; RUN_LIVE_CLAUDE_PERMISSION_TESTS=1 must be selected before binary discovery or invocation. Test results do not confer launch authority.
